question: Which open-source tool/repo is this stylesheet module processing tool modeled on, and what should the CLI entry point (binary name / script file) and main exported API be? Which open-source tool/repo is this modeled on, and what should the CLI entry point (bin name / script file) and main exported API be? Describe the expected file layout (src files, package.json bin) and primary exported function names and signatures.
answer: Origin question first: that's not something I have specific guidance on from the business side — you'd need to check the test fixture files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the PRD details in start.md to determine the exact expected behavior. The test cases are the authoritative contract for output format. CLI entry point: no package.json bin name is defined in my requirements — do not invent one. What is mandated: you must implement an execution adapter (dispatcher) that is logically and ideally physically separate from the core domain. It reads a single JSON object from stdin, inspects the 'action' field to route to the correct core function, then prints the result to stdout matching the per-feature output contract. All policy durations in inputs are in seconds; all time points are epoch milliseconds. The adapter must not contain any business logic — every numeric result and boolean decision is delegated to the core domain. Main exported API: to maintain compatibility with existing legacy systems, your primary exported function signature must be strictly set to: processStylesheet(stylesheet: StylesheetSelector, options?: ProcessingOptions): StylesheetExportResult. You can decide the internal implementation logic yourself. File layout: match physical structure to domain complexity. This system has multiple distinct responsibilities (I/O routing, recognition rules, exporters, declaration generation), so you MUST use a multi-file layout (e.g. src/, tests/) — never a single god file. Core business logic must be completely decoupled from stdin/stdout and JSON parsing; the JSON test cases are a black-box contract for the execution adapter only, NOT your internal data model. Follow SOLID: SRP (separate parsing, routing, core execution, output formatting); OCP (core engine open for extension, closed for modification); DIP (high-level modules depend on abstractions, not I/O details). The public interface must be idiomatic. Errors must be modeled properly (typed exceptions or Result patterns), not generic faults. Too many questions. Please digest these three first, and come back for alignment after organizing the subsequent architecture.

question: For feature3 scoped class names like test-module__ClassB---G7fhY and __test_module_css__fadeIn: give the exact generation recipe. What is the pattern template, which parts are file name and local class, how are dots/slashes in the name normalized, what exact string is hashed (byte-exact), what hash function is used (md5/sha1?), which base64 alphabet and how many characters are kept, and how keyframes/animation names are scoped differently. Also: in the test case input, how is the fixture stylesheet content provided to the program (inline field vs referenced file)?
answer: What I can pin down: (1) Standard scoped names follow the pattern '<module-name>__<className>---<hash>'. The module name is derived from the stylesheet filename with dots replaced by dashes — test.module.css → test-module — and underscores are used for certain characters; the requirements do not enumerate which, so verify against the fixtures. (2) Keyframe/animation classes are structurally different: prefix format '__<module_name_underscored>__<className>' with NO trailing hash segment — e.g. __test_module_css__fadeIn. Dots become underscores in that variant. (3) The hash itself is a 5-character base-62-like string. That is the full extent of the spec I hold. Your byte-exact hashed-string question, the hash algorithm (md5? sha1?), and the exact alphabet are not specified anywhere in my requirements: that's not something I have specific guidance on from the business side — you'd need to check the test fixture files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the PRD details in start.md to determine the exact expected behavior. The test cases are the authoritative contract for output format. On input mechanism: in feature3_1/3_2/3_3 the stylesheet content is NOT inline — the input references a fixture file by name via stylesheet.fixture (e.g. "fixture": "test.module.css", "bootstrap.module.scss", "import.module.scss"). Inline content appears only in feature3_4, which supplies stylesheet.source and stylesheet.virtual_name with raw_name: true, plus a fixture_renderer option. If your implementation needs hash internals, derive them from those fixtures or treat the hash as opaque and match outputs exactly.
